title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a connected Riemann surface. Theorem 2 constructs, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, the following data:
- a P^1-bundle P_X over X;
- a flat (integrable) connection on P_X;
- a section σ;
- an open subset X̃ ⊂ P_X containing σ(X);
- a map p: X̃ → X×X over X, with p∘σ = diagonal, compatible with the connections.
For each x, the fibre X̃_x → X is the universal cover based at x, embedded as a homogeneous domain of the fibre (P_X)_x ≅ P^1. In modern terms, X̃ → X×X is the fundamental groupoid Π_1(X), seen as a space over X×X via source and target. The pair (P_X, connection, σ) is the canonical uniformizing projective structure on X: a flat P^1-bundle with a section, i.e. an sl_2-oper. The developing map identifies each source fibre with a homogeneous domain in P^1. The whole construction is a 'relative', groupoid-theoretic restatement of the uniformization theorem.

This page splits into cases according to the universal cover.

Case 1: universal cover P^1. Every automorphism of P^1 has a fixed point, so the deck group is trivial and X = P^1. Then X̃ = X×X = P^1_X, p is the identity and the connection is trivial.

Case 2: universal cover the affine line E^1(C) = C.
- Fixed-point-free automorphisms of C are translations, so π_1 is a discrete subgroup of C of rank 0, 1 or 2. This gives X ≅ C, C* or an elliptic curve.
- In each case X carries a canonical algebraic structure, since analytic automorphisms are algebraic.
- Here X̃ = P_X − σ', where σ' is a horizontal section (the point at infinity of each fibre), disjoint from σ.
- Hence P_X is the projective closure of a vector bundle V with zero section σ.
- The flat connection preserves σ' but not σ. So it is an affine (Aff(1)) connection on V, not a linear one: 'la connexion de V n'induit pas la structure vectorielle'.

The next page identifies V with the tangent bundle T_X (conormal of σ = conormal of the diagonal = Ω^1). So X̃ ≅ T_X, i.e. the exponential/developing identification of the pointed universal cover with T_xX. The flat connection then becomes the canonical flat affine structure on X. Grothendieck then asks whether this connection is algebraic. By GAGA the question only arises for non-compact X (C, C*); he treats C and starts C*. The hyperbolic (disc) case presumably follows on later pages.

Purpose within cote 93: understanding the uniformizing differential equation (Schwarzian / Picard–Fuchs type) as a flat P^1-bundle, and its algebraicity, in the context of Gauss–Manin connections.
errors: The phrase 'à deux automorphismes … ont un point fixe' is garbled. The correct argument is simply that every nontrivial automorphism of P^1 has a fixed point, so no nontrivial group acts freely.
'X canoniquement muni d'une structure algébrique' is correct for C, C* and elliptic curves. It fails for the hyperbolic case, which is not covered here; e.g. the disc has no algebraic structure.
The page writes P_X = closure of V before identifying V. The fact that σ is not horizontal (so the connection is genuinely affine, not linear) is noted correctly. No substantive mathematical error.

ideas.what: Classification of Riemann surfaces with universal cover P^1 or C: P^1; C, C*, elliptic curves, via discrete translation subgroups of rank 0, 1, 2.
Family of pointed universal covers X̃ → X×X sitting inside a flat P^1-bundle with a section, giving the canonical projective structure on X.
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid with developing map; canonical (uniformizing) projective structure / sl_2-oper

ideas.what: In the parabolic case the flat P^1-bundle is the projective closure of the tangent bundle with an Aff(1)-connection, i.e. the canonical flat affine structure; the zero section is not horizontal.
ideas.modern_name: Affine structure on a Riemann surface as a flat Aff(1)-bundle (Gunning)

ideas.what: Question of the algebraicity of the uniformizing connection; compact case settled by GAGA.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity / regular singularity of the uniformizing oper; accessory parameter problem

missed.claim: A clean groupoid-theoretic packaging of uniformization: the whole family of pointed universal covers forms an open subspace of a flat P^1-bundle over X, mapping to X×X. This is a 'relative universal covering' formulation of the uniformizing projective structure. The mathematics is known (Gunning, opers), but this specific formulation, in the context of Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs, is not recorded as Grothendieck's.
missed.quote: Ici X̃ = P_X − σ', où σ' est une section horizontale de P_X ; donc, étant muni des deux sections analytiques σ, σ' disjointes, nous pouvons considérer P_X comme clôture projective d'un fibré vectoriel analytique V
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck around 1972 thinking of uniformization as a flat connection (essentially an oper) whose algebraicity he wanted to settle. This anticipates the oper viewpoint, though without new results.

deep.surprise_reason: The page treats only the elliptic and parabolic cases of uniformization, which are classical. The interest is the relative/groupoid formulation as a flat P^1-bundle (a projective structure / oper) and the algebraicity question, all of which is known in substance.
transcription_corrections: Case 2 heading should read 'Cas X̃ ≅ E^1(C) = C': E^1 is Grothendieck's notation for the affine line, used throughout the page.
Case 1 heading in the image reads roughly 'Cas X̃ = P^1_C(C)', with a corrected subscript.
'et à deux automorphismes … ont un point fixe' probably reads 'tout automorphisme analytique … a un point fixe au moins'.
'la connexion de V n'induit pas la structure vectorielle' likely means 'ne respecte pas' (does not preserve) the vector structure.

The left-margin diagonal note seems to begin 'La cat. des …' and contains 'algébriques', 'analytiques' and 'C, C*'. It is likely a remark on the equivalence between categories of algebraic and analytic objects in these cases; still largely illegible.
